neighbours.label: A speech verb that reports an answer to a question just asked ('I asked him why, and he said', 'she told me'); the same verb with no question before it stays quiet
fire: I asked the guard where the exit was, and he said it was closed.
We asked her about the plan and she said it was too late.
When she asked who was there, he told her it was only the cat.
I asked my father if he was tired, and he said yes.
She asks him what he wants, and Tom says he needs money.
They asked the driver why he stopped, and he said the road was blocked.
I asked the nurse how long it would take, and she told me an hour.
The teacher asked if anyone knew, and a boy said he did.
quiet: I walked past the guard at the exit, and he said it was closed.
We finished the plan and she said it was too late.
When she came home, he told her it was only the cat.
I sat with my father on the porch, and he said it was cold.
She brings him a coffee, and Tom says he needs money.
They stopped near the driver, and he said the road was blocked.
I waited by the nurse for a while, and she told me an hour.
The teacher walked in, and a boy said hello.

notes: Card: ' said' x6, '—' x4, ' says' x2, ' told' x2, '“Oh' x2, after 'I asked'. Probe: 'asked him why, and he said' 0.85, 'asked her ... she said' 0.78, 'she told' 0.54, 'Orhan says' 0.44; no question before: 'and he said' 0.00, 'she said hello' 0.04, 'The manager said' 0.01. ' he' before ' left' after a question reached 0.42, so the pole already reads the pronoun.
